Amber Environmental Sensor Specification

Section 1: Sampling Cadence

The Amber barometric sensor samples atmospheric pressure every 6 seconds in normal mode.

When battery charge falls below 18 percent, Amber switches to low-power mode and samples every 90 seconds.

Operational note 1 for amber-sensor (barometer-calibration): During routine shift handoffs, operators inspect the telemetry dashboard for amber-sensor across rack bay 11, verify that the ambient cooling intake stays within nominal seasonal tolerances, and confirm that weekly archive rotation completed before the midnight maintenance checklist. Capacity planning teams review rolling fourteen-day utilization charts for barometer-calibration, comparing peak burst volume against provisioned headroom and noting any scheduled firmware staging windows in the regional calendar. Incident commanders keep printed escalation trees beside the console desk and record routine drill timestamps in the shared station logbook without modifying active production parameters or altering steady-state routing weights.

Operational note 2 for amber-sensor (enclosure-seals): During routine shift handoffs, operators inspect the telemetry dashboard for amber-sensor across rack bay 12, verify that the ambient cooling intake stays within nominal seasonal tolerances, and confirm that weekly archive rotation completed before the midnight maintenance checklist. Section 2: Alert Escalation Thresholds

Amber emits a critical dew-point alert when relative humidity exceeds 88 percent for ten consecutive minutes.

Amber monitors relative humidity continuously to detect condensation risk.

Operational note 3 for amber-sensor (humidity-drift): During routine shift handoffs, operators inspect the telemetry dashboard for amber-sensor across rack bay 13, verify that the ambient cooling intake stays within nominal seasonal tolerances, and confirm that weekly archive rotation completed before the midnight maintenance checklist. Section 3: Firmware Flash Procedure

Over-the-air firmware images must be verified against the pinned ECDSA-P256 root before reboot.
